title: The Smallest Car That Can Take Every Trip

concept.title: Turn every trip into two events — passengers +p at the start and -p at the end — and sweep along the road
body: A car drives along a road in one direction. Each trip says: `p` passengers get in at the point `a` and get out at the point `b`. The car never turns back. What is the **smallest number of seats** the car needs so that it can carry all the trips? For the trips `(2, 1, 5)`, `(3, 3, 7)` the car holds 2 passengers between the points 1 and 3, and 5 between 3 and 5, so it needs 5 seats.

The number of passengers in the car changes only at the endpoints of the trips. Make **two events** for every trip: `(a, +p)` and `(b, -p)`. Sort the events by their position; at one position put the **negative events first** (the passengers who get out leave before the new ones enter, so the car is never counted as fuller than it is). Walk through the events, keep the current load, and remember the **largest load** seen.

body.code:
events = []
for p, a, b in trips:
    events.append((a, p))
    events.append((b, -p))
events.sort()                          # at the same position -p comes before +p
load = peak = 0
for pos, delta in events:
    load += delta
    peak = max(peak, load)
print(peak)

body: The answer is the maximum, over all points of the road, of the total number of passengers whose trip covers the point. The sweep costs O(n log n) for the sort. The same event-sweep idea answers "how many meetings are happening at once" and, with weights, "how much of a resource is in use at the same time".

statement: `n` trips are given. In the trip `i`, `p` passengers get into the car at the point `a` and get out at the point `b` of a straight road, which the car drives along in one direction. Passengers who get out at a point leave before the passengers who get in at the same point enter. Print the smallest number of seats the car needs for all the trips.
inputFormat: The first line has `n`: the number of trips.
Each of the next `n` lines has three numbers `p`, `a` and `b`: the number of passengers, the point where they get in and the point where they get out.
outputFormat: Print the smallest number of seats.
constraints: Passengers who get out at a point leave before the passengers who get in at that point enter.

examples.note: Between the points 3 and 5 there are 2 + 3 = 5 passengers: 5.
The first group leaves at 3 before the second enters: 6.

hints: Create two events per trip: +p at the start and -p at the end.
Sort the events by position; at equal positions the negative ones come first.
The answer is the largest running sum.

explanation: Every trip adds the events +p at its start and -p at its end; the events are sorted (ends before starts at equal positions) and the largest running sum is the answer.
solution.complexity: Time O(n log n), space O(n).

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n = int(input())
trips = [list(map(int, input().split())) for _ in range(n)]

events = []
for p, a, b in trips:
    events.append((a, p))
    events.append((b, -p))
events.sort()
load = peak = 0
for pos, delta in events:
    load += delta
    if load > peak:
        peak = load
print(peak)
